v4.9.078 - a quick little mark stays a mark (#361)

#361 Roman: "when I'm in scribble mode and paint really quick, sometimes a stroke
     I draw disappears immediately after I make it. Is it because I draw too
     fast?" And then, better than my own guess: "could it have something to do
     with what we introduced for drawing a dot?"

     It could, and it did.

     When the pen comes up the app decides: tap, or line? A tap becomes a dot. It
     decided with two tests - under 400ms, and never more than THIRTY pixels from
     where it started. Not the length of the line drawn: how far it ever got from
     its beginning. So a quick tick, a small circle, a short dash curving back on
     itself was called a tap. The mark was thrown away and a dot put at the start
     point. A stroke vanishing the instant it is made, and only when you are
     quick, because a slower mark passed the time test. A finger had it worst: a
     finger was allowed thirty pixels, a pencil eight.

     Speed says nothing about what a person meant. Movement does. A tap is now a
     finger that did not move - eight pixels of wobble, the same for a finger as
     for a pencil - and how long it rested there does not matter. Anything that
     travelled is a mark and is kept whole, beginning and end.

#362 NOT SHIPPED, AND DELIBERATELY SO.

     A second, separate fault, found while looking for the first and caught by a
     test of its own: every time the 3x2 page is drawn the app throws the whole
     scribble layer away and rebuilds it, so a sync arriving mid-stroke destroys
     the canvas under the hand.

     Three attempts at the fix, three failures - holding the layer, then holding
     the page, then holding the whole redraw - each leaving the layer not rebuilt
     at all. Taken out rather than poked at further. The test stays in the file,
     marked as still open, so it is not forgotten.

     One piece kept: the scribble layer now SAYS when the pen is down. Nothing
     acts on it for the page, but the version-drawing canvas has honoured that
     flag for a while, so a picture finishing its decode can no longer repaint
     over a stroke in progress.

THE SIMULATOR CAN SCRIBBLE

Real pointer events on the real overlay: a stroke, a quick tick with a finger, a
pen held down across a sync, and readers for how many strokes a frame holds and
how far the last one travelled. Three tests, two green.

Two wrong reproductions on the way, both found by the test rather than by Roman:
a dozen strokes with no pause at all (they all land before a single push starts,
so nothing is ever in flight), and the other device sitting idle (with nobody
else working every pull comes back empty and nothing is ever rebuilt). Both are
now guarded against in the test itself, so it cannot pass for the wrong reason.

21 of 22 pass. The one failure is the random day, which now disagrees on two
different seeds - 985927 and 511151 - in the same way: after one device is away
while the other rearranges, they end with the frames in a different order and one
frame carrying older writing. Repeatable, and older than any of today's work.
That is the next hunt.
